profile.reading:
Per CoreSite's own facility page, this building, SV9, is located at 2915 Stender Way, Santa Clara, CA 95054, the newest building on CoreSite's nine-building Silicon Valley campus, completed and announced in July 2025. Square footage varies across CoreSite's own materials: the completion press release and current facility page state 228,000-plus square feet, while an earlier 2022-2023 construction-approval release and the spec-sheet landing page cite 200,000 square feet, reflecting the difference between the planned and as-built figures; the more recent 228,000-plus figure is treated as authoritative here. SV9 is CoreSite's only Silicon Valley building with a published MW figure: 34 critical megawatts, per the construction-approval press release. The building participates in the NVIDIA DGX-Ready Data Center program alongside CoreSite's general SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA compliance claims.

CoreSite's Santa Clara sub-campus (SV3 through SV9) is described in a CoreSite construction-approval release as exceeding 775,000 square feet combined, part of a nine-building, 1.4-million-plus-square-foot Silicon Valley presence. CoreSite is a subsidiary of American Tower Corporation (NYSE: AMT), which completed its acquisition of CoreSite in late 2021; Stonepeak Partners LP separately acquired roughly 29% to 36% of American Tower's US data center business in 2022.

American Tower reported record leasing at CoreSite driving stronger-than-expected second-quarter 2026 results, projecting data-center segment revenue of $1.20 billion to $1.22 billion for full-year 2026, roughly 14.9% growth at the midpoint, and raising its full-year outlook on the strength of that performance in part due to demand for newer, AI-ready capacity like SV9; the company budgeted approximately $695 million in data-center development spending for 2026.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CoreSite was founded in 2001 as CRG West, a Carlyle Group portfolio company, beginning operations at two West Coast carrier hotel buildings, Market Post Tower and One Wilshire, both in Los Angeles. The firm rebranded from CRG West to CoreSite in June 2009 and completed an IPO in September 2010. American Tower Corporation, the public tower and infrastructure company (NYSE: AMT, SEC CIK 1053507), completed its acquisition of CoreSite in December 2021. Stonepeak Partners LP later bought roughly 29 percent of American Towers US data center business directly in July 2022, increasing that stake to about 36 percent by October 2022. CoreSites own current Silicon Valley regional page (operator source, tier-1, https://www.coresite.com/data-center-locations/silicon-valley) names nine data centers on this Santa Clara campus, SV1 through SV9, totaling more than 1.4 million square feet campus wide, but only describes SV1, SV2, SV4, SV7, SV8, and SV9 individually, SV1 and SV2 are not rows in this registry. SV3, SV5, and SV6 are not detailed on that page, so their building specific facts below come from data center industry aggregator directories instead. CoreSites own regional page gives this specific building, SV9, an address of 2915 Stender Way, Santa Clara, CA 95054, with 228,000 plus square feet. Baxtel adds that CoreSite acquired this parcel in April 2019 as a 3.8 acre site with an existing office building, with data center development expected after then current leases expired, acquisition history that does not conflict with the operators own current address and square footage. No MW or power capacity figure was found for this specific building in any source checked this session.

reading.body:
CoreSite SV9 is a 228,000-square-foot building completed in July 2025 on CoreSite's nine-building Silicon Valley campus in Santa Clara County. The operator publishes 34 critical megawatts of IT capacity for this building alone, making it the largest single facility by published power in California outside the top 11 and placing it in the state's 12th rank. Assuming 40 kilowatts per rack as a common AI training density, 34 megawatts of IT load translates to roughly 850 racks, though the operator's published figure does not specify mix or actual tenant deployment.

The building holds SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA certifications, qualifying it for regulated workloads and enterprise security requirements. It is also designated NVIDIA DGX-Ready, indicating it is engineered to host NVIDIA's latest accelerator platforms. These certifications describe what the facility is designed to host, not which tenants currently occupy it.

American Tower Corporation, which acquired CoreSite in late 2021, reported in mid-2026 that CoreSite was leasing record capacity driven by demand for AI-ready facilities like SV9, citing this newer capacity in its decision to raise full-year 2026 guidance and budget roughly $695 million in data center development spending. SV9's published power and recent completion during a period of elevated AI infrastructure demand place it within the operator's stated growth narrative, though its actual utilization and tenant commitments are not published.
